notes:
Account summary:
- Large payments platform, heavy fraud-detection & reconciliation workloads. Looking to move from a mix of hosted APIs + intermittent on-prem GPUs to a predictable dedicated plan for inference at scale.
- Primary ask: guaranteed throughput for peak trading hours, p95 latency SLOs, and unit economics per token for committed GPU reserves.
Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-12 discovery call (Sofia/Diego) — initial requirements: 200 concurrent chat sessions, embeddings for 3TB docs, reranking for trade signals.
- 2026-01-22 architecture deep-dive — security asked about KMS, network egress, audit logs.
- 2026-02-10 onsite benchmark (ff-20260210-1147) — 3 test suites: chat latency, embedding throughput, rerank p99.
- 2026-02-15 POC start — Redwood provided 4 H100-equivalent nodes for 2-week POC.
POC & cost modeling (notes / numbers):
- Commitment scenarios modeled: 6-month vs 12-month vs no-commit (on-demand).
- GPU baseline used: NVIDIA H100 80GB equivalent (for modeling). Price examples (internal): 6-mo commit -> $120k/mo for 8 reserved GPUs; 12-mo commit -> $95k/mo for same capacity (volume discount).
- Utilization assumptions: conservative 55% effective utilization (safety/burst buffer), realistic 70% (with batching & KV caching), optimistic 85% (tight scheduling + steady streams).
- Unit economics: computed token-level cost after batching & caching:
   * 70% utilization scenario -> approx $0.00035 per generated token (end-to-end, includes infra & ops).
   * 55% utilization scenario -> approx $0.00048 per token.
   * No-commit / hosted pricing observed in POC comparisons -> ~ $0.0011 - $0.0014 per token depending on model size.
- Break-even calculus: with 8 reserved GPUs at $95k/mo (12-mo), monthly break-even token volume ~ 270B tokens (assumes 70% util, average request 300 tokens returned).
- Sensitivity: unit cost increases ~25-35% if KV cache hit rate drops below 40% or batching falls short during peak spikes.
Throughput & latency SLO targets discussed:
- Target p95 latency: <= 150ms for 256-token chat responses (internal goal).
- Peak throughput: sustain 120k tokens/sec aggregated across GPUs during market open.
- SLA asks: 99.95% uptime, SLA credits tied to p95 latency breaches, scheduled maintenance windows capped at 2 hours/month.
Negotiation/contract points flagged:
- Wants explicit fallback policy: if Dedicated capacity degraded, automatic routing to Redwood hosted compatible model with defined cost & rate limits.
- Request to include rolling upgrade windows and advance notice for kernel-level changes.
- Security/legal: addendum for EU data residency + audit-log access for 2 years.
Open technical questions (from security/infra):
- HSM/KMS integration detail and key rotation policy; proof-of-concept for audit log pipeline.
- Network egress and peering for hybrid on-prem/offload flows.
- Model licensing language: who owns fine-tuned checkpoints? customer wants clear clause.
Stakeholder quotes / shorthand from calls:
- "We need predictable unit economics — spikes are fine as long as the math works across the month." — Head of Infrastructure.
- "Latency SLO is non-negotiable for trade alerts; p95 breach = immediate escalation." — Product lead.
Next steps (short):
- SE to deliver revised pricing workbook reflecting 6 vs 12 month commit + utilization bands (due 2026-03-05).
- Legal to receive draft SLA and data residency addendum (Sofia to introduce).
- Security to receive KMS/HSM integration summary + SOC2 artifacts (via drive link).
- Procurement meeting scheduled w/ finance: 2026-03-09 (tentative).
CRM-style action items:
- Assign CSM if deal goes to procurement (TBD).
- Track INF-4123 for internal infra questions; escalate SEC-2891 to security eng.
- Note: prioritise demonstration of caching benefits (show 40%+ reduction in per-token compute) during next POC run.
